reference_boundary: Official Codex glossary source docs are citation metadata and terminology references only. This manifest does not make Codex product surfaces mandatory for ADK runtimes or enable compatibility defaults.

terms.definition_boundary: A worker that reasons over context, uses tools and completes a task.
terms.adk_usage: Use for a runtime actor or role, not for every skill or workflow document.

terms.definition_boundary: Reusable workflow package with instructions and optional scripts or references.
terms.adk_usage: Use for reusable task workflows with metadata and progressive disclosure.

terms.definition_boundary: Installable bundle that can distribute skills, tools and integrations.
terms.adk_usage: Use only for installable bundles, not plain skills or manifests.

terms.definition_boundary: External tool or context provider exposed through MCP.
terms.adk_usage: Use only when a live MCP transport or declared connector exists.

terms.definition_boundary: Scheduled or recurring task; a thread automation is a recurring wake-up attached to an existing thread.
terms.adk_usage: Use for scheduled/report-only runs with cadence, stop condition and first-run review.

terms.definition_boundary: Specialized child agent spawned to work on part of a task.
terms.adk_usage: Use for delegated child execution with explicit scope_read, scope_write and integration ownership.

terms.definition_boundary: Mode where changes are isolated in a separate Git worktree.
terms.adk_usage: Use only when a real Git worktree or equivalent isolated checkout is used.

terms.definition_boundary: Named least-privilege policy combining filesystem and network rules.
terms.adk_usage: Use for runtime permission presets; do not confuse with skill/profile catalogs.

must_not: call a skill bundle a plugin unless it is installable
call report-only scripts automations without cadence and stop condition
claim worktree isolation without a real worktree or equivalent checkout

ambiguous_usage_checks: agent must refer to a runtime actor or role
skill must refer to a reusable workflow package
plugin must refer to an installable bundle
automation must include cadence and stop condition
worktree must refer to a real isolated checkout
permission profile must refer to filesystem and network runtime policy
